title: Spotting image flaws and garbled text

sections.skill: Inspect a generated image for visual errors and garbled text

questions.prompt: Which part of a generated image often has errors?

choices.text: The overall color of the sky, which image tools always get wrong in every picture

questions.intro: Generated images often contain FLAWS that are easy to miss at a glance. Look closely at HANDS and FINGERS (extra, missing or bent oddly), EYES and TEETH, OBJECTS that melt into each other, SHADOWS and REFLECTIONS that do not match the light, and PATTERNS that break, such as a fence that changes shape. TEXT inside images is a common problem: letters may be garbled, words misspelled ("Bake Sael"), or numbers changed. Before using an image, zoom in, read every word letter by letter, and fix or remove what is wrong. Often it is easier to add text yourself in a design app.

sections.skill: Inspect an image with a checklist

questions.prompt: Six fingers on a waving hand fails which point?
questions.intro: Use a five-point checklist. (1) BODIES: count fingers, check eyes, teeth and limbs. (2) OBJECTS: look for things blending together or floating. (3) LIGHT: do shadows fall the same way? (4) PATTERNS: do fences, tiles and stripes stay consistent? (5) TEXT: read every word letter by letter, and check dates and numbers. Example: a picture shows a person waving with six fingers, a cup merging into a table, and a sign reading "Opne." That fails points 1, 2 and 5.

sections.title: Apply it

questions.prompt: Which flaw matters most on an event flyer?
questions.intro: Some flaws matter more than others. A slightly odd cloud is harmless; a wrong date or price on a flyer is not. A misspelled name on a certificate or a wrong phone number on a poster can cause real problems. Small symbols, such as safety signs or logos, may look almost right but be wrong or belong to someone else. Check where the image will be seen: details that look fine on a phone can be obvious when printed large.
